canonical_statement: For a probability measure P and a sequence of measurable events A_n: if A_n is increasing, then P(A_n) tends to P(union_n A_n), and if A_n is decreasing, then P(A_n) tends to P(intersection_n A_n).
domain_and_universes: universe u; Omega : Type u; MeasurableSpace Omega; P : Measure Omega; IsProbabilityMeasure P; A : Nat -> Set Omega; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: Monotone A for continuity from below
Antitone A for continuity from above
conclusion: The ENNReal-valued sequence n |-> P (A n) tends atTop to the measure of the indexed union in the increasing case and to the measure of the indexed intersection in the decreasing case.
historical_relationship: The checked implication maps the canonical all-measurable event formulation to the historical candidate's broader NullMeasurableSet formulation for the decreasing branch. The reverse implication is deliberately uncredited because null-measurable sets need not be measurable in the original measurable space.
